God told Joshua, "As I was with Moses, so I will be with you." How does God's faithfulness carry from one generation to the next?
"Be strong and courageous... for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go." Where do you need courage today?
God told Joshua to meditate on the law day and night. How can you keep God's word in your mind?
The people promised to follow Joshua as they had Moses. How can you support those God puts in leadership?
Rahab hid the spies at great risk. What gave her courage?
Rahab said, "The Lord your God, he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath." How did she come to believe?
The scarlet cord marked Rahab's house for safety. How does this picture God's rescue?
The ark went ahead of the people. How does God go ahead of you?
The priests had to step into the water before it stopped. Where might God be asking you to step out in faith?
The people crossed on dry ground. When has God made a way for you?
Twelve stones were set up as a memorial. What memorials help you remember God's work?
The stones were so all the earth would know the Lord's hand is mighty. Who could you tell about God's power?
The kings' hearts melted when they heard what God had done. What does it show that God's works are seen by others?
The manna stopped when they ate the fruit of the land. How does God provide in different ways at different times?
The commander of the Lord's army said, "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy." What does it mean to be on God's side?
God's battle plan for Jericho seemed strange. When has God asked you to trust his way over yours?
The walls fell after they obeyed. What does this show about faith and obedience?
Rahab and her family were saved. What does this show about God's mercy to outsiders?
Israel was defeated because of hidden sin. How can hidden sin affect others?
Achan confessed: "I coveted them and took them." How does coveting lead to sin?
Sin brought trouble on the whole community. Why does God take sin so seriously?
God said, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed." How does God encourage after failure?
Joshua read all the words of the law to everyone. Why is it important to hear all of God's word together?
Israel did not ask counsel from the Lord before making a treaty. What decisions do you need to bring to God?
Joshua kept his word even though they had been deceived. What does this teach about integrity?
God fought for Israel. How has God fought for you?
The sun stood still at Joshua's prayer. What does this show about God's power?
"Do not be afraid or dismayed; be strong and courageous." What do you need courage for?
God said, "Do not be afraid of them." What fear is God speaking into?
Joshua left nothing undone of all the Lord commanded Moses. What would complete obedience look like for you?
"And the land had rest from war." What rest has God given you?
The victories under Moses are remembered. How does remembering past victories build faith?
A long list of kings defeated. What does this list show about God keeping his promise?
There was still much land to possess. What areas of your life still need to be given to God?
The Lord was the inheritance of the Levites. What does it mean for God to be your inheritance?
"The Lord God of Israel is their inheritance." How does this speak to what matters most?
Caleb wholly followed the Lord. What does wholehearted faith look like?
At 85, Caleb said, "Give me this hill country." What does his courage in old age teach you?
Caleb received his inheritance because he followed the Lord fully. How does God honour faithfulness?
Judah's borders were set out. What does this detail show about God's care in keeping promises?
Achsah asked her father for springs of water. What do you need to ask your Father for?
Judah could not drive out the Jebusites. What does incomplete obedience lead to?
Joseph's descendants received their inheritance. How does God keep his promises across generations?
They did not drive out the Canaanites. Where might you be settling for less than God's best?
The daughters of Zelophehad received what God had promised. What does this show about God's faithfulness?
Joshua told the tribe to clear the forest and take the land. Where might God be calling you to work hard for what he gives?
The tabernacle was set up at Shiloh. Why is God's presence at the centre of the land?
Joshua asked, "How long will you put off going in?" What are you putting off that God wants you to do?
Simeon's inheritance was within Judah. How does God provide even when things look different from what we expect?
Joshua received his inheritance last. What does this show about his leadership?
Cities of refuge protected those who killed by accident. How is Jesus our refuge?
The cities were spread throughout the land so anyone could reach one. What does this show about God's grace being near?
The Levites were given cities among all the tribes. How can God's servants bless every community?
"Not one word of all the good promises... had failed; all came to pass." What promise of God have you seen fulfilled?
Joshua urged them to love the Lord and serve him with all their heart. What does this look like for you?
The tribes almost went to war over a misunderstanding. How can you avoid jumping to conclusions?
The altar was a witness that "the Lord is God." How do you show you belong to the Lord?
"It is the Lord your God who has fought for you." How has God fought for you?
"Be very careful, therefore, to love the Lord your God." Why does love for God need care?
"Not one word has failed of all the good things that the Lord your God promised." How does this encourage you?
Joshua retold God's story from Abraham to the land. How would you tell the story of what God has done for you?
"Choose this day whom you will serve... as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord." What would it mean for you to say this?
The people said, "We will serve the Lord." What makes that promise hard to keep?
Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua. How does a faithful leader influence others?
